questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. If an item is too small for its label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie the item with other hazardous materials and place a label sheet on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box that has a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Shippers must place diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on most hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing while transporting chlorine, what must you do?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross without stopping if no warning lights are flashing.
You can cross without stopping if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.

questions.question: If your cargo containing hazardous materials is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, do not drive longer than necessary for safety. Continuing to drive spreads contamination. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with it, and get help.

questions.question: Generally, what must a shipping paper list?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the route.

questions.correctAnswerText: An emergency response telephone number.
questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are some exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Contact emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Contact emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires require special training and equipment. Unless you have this training, let emergency personnel handle the fire.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials cargo tanks, what must you do at railroad crossings?

options.text: Cross the tracks without slowing or stopping.
Slow down, but you are not required to stop.
Stop at railroad crossings before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at railroad crossings before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with tanks used for hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the tanks are empty.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park the vehicle?

options.text: For only short periods of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Except when parking briefly for necessary vehicle operations like refueling, never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Never park within five feet of the road. Park only briefly.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading or unloading must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a chemical suit.
questions.explanation: The supervisor overseeing cargo tank loading or unloading must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet of it, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed. Wearing a chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: If a package contains liquid containers, what must the box display?

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages containing liquid containers must have orientation markers. Arrows on the box must point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: If you discover that your cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If you discover a leak, identify the materials using the shipping papers, labels, or package location. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: The National Response Center must be notified of an incident resulting in any of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Injury not requiring hospitalization.
questions.explanation: The National Response Center must be notified if an incident causes death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, evacuation of the public, or closure of a major route for more than one hour. It must also be notified for fire, spillage, or suspected contamination involving radiation, bacteria, or toxins. If the driver believes the situation is serious, it should be reported.

questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reportable quantity
questions.explanation: On a shipping paper, the letters "RQ" can be used instead of an "X" in the "HM" column. This marks a reportable quantity of hazardous material.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, the shipper should provide which placard?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If the shipping paper or package shows "Inhalation Hazard," you must use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: When traveling with Division 1.1 explosives, you may park no closer than ____ from the nearest building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you cannot park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. The only exception is if you park for a short time for an operational need, such as refueling.

questions.question: If a driver stops and leaves their vehicle while transporting hazardous materials, the shipping papers should be:

options.text: Left in the front seat of the cab.
Placed in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left in the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: If a driver exits the vehicle, hazardous materials shipping papers must stay on the driver's seat.

questions.question: In the Hazardous Materials Table, Column 2 lists:
questions.correctAnswerText: The names of materials.
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table shows the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: Placarded vehicles must carry fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: In general, before loading or unloading any flammable liquids, an engine should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need the engine running to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening the fill hole and keep it grounded until after closing the fill hole.

questions.question: Flammable gases are categorized as ____ hazards.
questions.correctAnswerText: Class 2
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are assigned to hazardous materials Class 2.

questions.question: On a shipping paper, if the letter "G" appears in Column 1, what else needs to appear?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging containing the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (meaning "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, you must also list the technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others when transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Display HazMat placards on the truck.
Install flashing lights on the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Display HazMat placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Shippers must also provide labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which is NOT recommended?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use a hook.
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers or packaging when loading hazardous materials.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take hazardous materials training courses.
questions.explanation: The manual is a starting point. To learn more, read federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials and attend training courses.

questions.question: Which sign suggests a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
Your last pickup was labeled hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: If the shipper is in a business involving hazardous materials, the shipment may be hazardous. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control businesses, agricultural suppliers, and dealers in explosives, munitions, or fireworks.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placard?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the correct placard, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park at least ____ from any building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, gathering place, or open fire.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials cannot be transported in a trailer with:
questions.correctAnswerText: A heater.
questions.explanation: Heaters are not permitted in the same space as Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: What could indicate a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting these items.

questions.question: A person supervising the loading of a tank must:

options.text: Not necessarily be able to move the vehicle.
Not know about the materials being loaded.
Stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must supervise loading and unloading. They must stay alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.
